name: append-only-event-log-with-seq-by-append
what: The session is an append-only event log; append assigns `seq = session.events.length` itself, so an event that arrives with seq undefined can never be hidden by ANY mechanism. Every removal is expressed as a projection marker rather than a rewrite, which is what makes a resumed session a pure replay of the log.
invariants: The raw log is never rewritten or truncated
Unkeyed events (seq undefined) are permanently visible
failurePolicy: fail-closed at the write boundary (append throws on a foreign source on assistant/message packages and on non-canonical base64 / unsupported media type / oversize images) and deliberately fail-safe on read (every projection degrades on malformed persisted events)

name: derivemessages-wire-shape-enforcement
what: deriveMessages is the single model-visible projection and it enforces the wire shape of a step as one unit: tool/call events are buffered and flushed as assistant(content, toolCalls) followed by the tool results (never interleaved), the step's assistant/message folds INTO the same assistant message, a mid-step user/message is deferred until after that block, and step/end flushes so consecutive steps never merge into role-alternation-breaking runs.
invariants: Function call blocks always precede their outputs
Role alternation is preserved across step boundaries
failurePolicy: read-side fail-safe: malformed persisted shapes (e.g. a truthy non-array output.images) must not throw out of the projection

name: jsonl-backend-with-atomic-rewrite-and-torn-tail-recovery
what: One file per session: header line 0 (JSON SessionMeta) plus one JSON event per line. Parsing takes the contiguous committed prefix and stops at the first unparsable line while a separate probe detects a torn final line; every whole-file rewrite is temp file (wx) + write + fsync + rename with best-effort directory fsync, and an append writes at the committed byte offset and on failure truncates back to the previous committed size so a clean retry cannot duplicate seqs. This backend owns STRUCTURAL repair (truncate + synthetic closers); the semantic tool-result repair lives in session-persistence.
invariants: Path safety is enforced in one artifactPath helper: a posix-absolute id, a win32-rooted id or a path resolving outside the store root is rejected
updateMeta replaces ONLY line 0 and keeps every event line byte-exact
failurePolicy: fail-closed on writes (append failure rolls back and rethrows, create uses flag wx, an out-of-root id throws) and tolerant on reads (a torn tail truncates to the committed prefix)

name: coordinator-load-gate-version-refusal-before-repair
what: load reads the file, runs assertVersionSupported (refuse newer-than-build; refuse a hole in the upgrade chain) and only THEN calls backend.repair, because read is non-destructive while repair may truncate and rewrite. The same gate refuses unknown event types unless they carry ignorable:true (deprecated and dropped) or were registered via registerEventType; the package registers its own set of new event types at module init so a persistence-only path still loads team/*, todo/write, goal/change, job/status, schedule/change, agent/input/*, session/title, plan/mode, subagent/*, reasoning, command/* and rewind/point. rewind/point is deliberately NOT ignorable because dropping it would silently resurrect rewound turns.
invariants: The one operation that can destroy data must be unreachable for a file this build does not understand
Hide-markers are never treated as ignorable
failurePolicy: fail-closed: unsupported/newer format and a missing upgrade path throw SessionFormatUnsupportedError; an unknown non-ignorable event type is refused

name: write-behind-with-failure-retention-and-quiescence-barrier
what: Appends are batched to the backend by fixed-deadline write-behind: on a failed write the batch is put back at the FRONT of the queue and the automatic timer is paused until new work arrives, so a background failure neither loses events nor spins. flush() cancels the wait and drains through a barrier that never rejects the producer, because a producer must not be failed by durability it did not await.
invariants: A failed batch is re-queued ahead of newer events (no reordering)
flush() never rejects its caller
failurePolicy: fail-soft by design: background flush failures go to reportBackgroundFailure, documents report but never reject the caller, close() is best-effort allSettled

name: tail-only-log-semantic-crash-repair
what: A PURE, DETERMINISTIC, TAIL-ONLY repair layer above the backend's structural repair adds a synthetic TOOL_ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH tool/result for every unmatched tool/call in the LAST turn and closes an open step/turn. Earlier turns are never touched and the input array is never mutated, keeping the raw log replayable byte-for-byte. Without it a crash mid-tool replays assistant(toolCalls) with no tool responses, which breaks Messages-API alternation on continue.
invariants: Repair is tail-only and pure (no input mutation)
A synthetic result is marked as aborted-before-dispatch, never as a fabricated success
failurePolicy: fail-soft / integrity-preserving: repair only adds closers and markers; nothing is deleted

name: session-ownership-lease-os-byte-range-lock
what: One process holds a process-lifetime EXCLUSIVE OS byte-range lock on a per-session lock file (Win32 LockFileEx via koffi / Linux flock), acquired non-blocking with a JS backoff retry until a deadline, released idempotently. The OS auto-releases on process death so there is no stale-lock problem; the lock path is derived only from the session id as <storeRoot>/.i-harness-locks/<sha256(sessionId).slice(0,24)>.lock. Only win32 and linux ship bindings; any other platform (including darwin) fails closed with SessionLockUnsupportedError and no weaker lockfile+PID fallback is shipped.
invariants: Non-blocking at the OS level; the wait lives in JS
No weaker fallback is shipped for unsupported platforms
failurePolicy: fail-closed throughout: a live conflicting holder past the deadline throws SessionLockConflictError, an unsupported platform or missing native backend throws SessionLockUnsupportedError, any non-conflict OS failure throws immediately

name: fork-with-source-coordinate-marker-remapping
what: Fork seeds a child session with a completed-turn prefix from the source and applies the SOURCE's own hidden-region semantics in the child's coordinate space: rewind windows are extended back to the anchor turn's turn/start, rewind/point markers are DROPPED (a copied marker would assert a phantom cut over events the child never had), compaction markers are KEPT, and the kept events are renumbered with shadowedSeqs/removedSeqs/messageSeqs remapped. The child therefore sees exactly what the parent's model saw.
invariants: Markers are never copied verbatim across a coordinate change
Only complete turns are copied (completed-turn prefix)
failurePolicy: fail-closed: SessionForkUnavailableError when the backend cannot support the fork

name: session-listing-blank-probe-and-title-projection
what: Session discovery is served by the JSONL backend's list/profile surface plus session-title: profile() is honest-bounding rather than exact (an artifact at or under 1024 bytes is read whole for the exact blank answer; a larger one is served blank:false WITHOUT reading the body, and its header is read from a capped 64 KiB window on line 0). Titles come from session-title, which appends a session/title event (latest-wins projection) and mirrors a namespaced document for cheap list screens.
invariants: The blank probe never guesses: 'may have content', never 'is blank'
Only real user messages are eligible title inputs (any user/message carrying a source is excluded)
failurePolicy: fail-soft: provider title suggestion degrades to a deterministic word-count fallback, and the document mirror write is fired-and-caught

name: append-only-jsonl-event-log
what: Session holds an in-memory append-only `SessionEvent[]` written only by `Session.append` (packages/core/session/src/index.ts:703-754): each call snapshots `data` as lossless JSON, validates the event payload and surface metadata, freezes the envelope, and pushes it, so the event's `seq` is exactly the pre-push log length. The JSONL backend serializes those events one JSON object per line after a `type:'session'` header record (`eventLines`/`eventLine`, session-persistence-jsonl/src/format.ts:312-323) into an immutable generation file `session.v<N>.jsonl` (optionally checksummed Zstandard frames), extending it with `persistBatch` (index.ts:807-821) or materializing a fresh generation. Cold reads decode the artifact through a bounded parsed-log handoff memo (`COLD_LOG_MEMO_MAX_ENTRIES = 2`) and one fail-closed validation pass (`decodeStoredLog`, index.ts:711-768).
invariants: Committed events are never rewritten and seq is contiguous from 0, equal to the log length (the `seq = log.length` contract)
Every event's `data` must be losslessly JSON-serializable; violations throw at the append site rather than at flush time
One JSON object per event row, with the header as exactly one JSONL line, so a physical tail is truncatable at a record boundary
failurePolicy: fail-closed — non-JSON payloads, invalid surface metadata, and reentrant appends throw before the log mutates (index.ts:713-735); unreadable artifact bytes become SessionPersistenceCorruptionError (index.ts:751)
constants: SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION = 3 stamped into every header line (packages/core/session/src/types.ts:88)

name: seq-contiguity-and-branded-sequence-types
what: Sequence positions are nominal types rather than bare numbers: `SessionSeq` admits only non-negative safe integers that are existing event positions and `SessionLogOffset` admits the same for gaps/prefix lengths/cursors, both rejecting `-0` (packages/core/session/src/types.ts:30-58). Contiguity is enforced at three boundaries with the same rule: the Session constructor refuses a seed whose `seq` differs from its index (index.ts:570-572), every append derives `seq` from the log length, and the persistence seam re-checks batches with `assertContiguous(id, events, cursor)` before writing (session-persistence/src/storage-contract.ts:145-151).
invariants: Stored and live logs are dense from seq 0; a gap is never representable except through the explicit `SessionLogOffset` gap/prefix type
A seed, fork prefix, or append batch must continue the stored next-seq exactly
`-0` is not a valid sequence value anywhere (JSON-unstable negative zero)
failurePolicy: fail-closed — TypeError from the brand constructors, `seed event at index N has seq M (expected N)` from the constructor, and `append seq mismatch` from assertContiguous

name: surface-projection-and-derived-history-cache
what: The model-visible conversation is a projection over the event log rather than a stored field: message-producing events carry a `surfaceOp` (`'append'` or `{op:'replace',startSeq,endSeq}`) and `sourceEventSeqs` (packages/core/session/src/types.ts:434-450), and `SurfaceManager.validateNext` accepts each candidate before it enters the log. `Session.deriveMessages()` walks the ordered surface nodes and folds the pure per-node rule `deriveEventMessage` (surface.ts:92-126), caching each node's projection exactly once and rebuilding only when the surface's `replaceGeneration` changes (index.ts:825-846). The same exported fold is reused by external reconstructors so a rebuilt transcript equals what the request was built from.
invariants: Derived history comes only from surface nodes; a raw event without a marker never enters the transcript
A replacement node must cite every shadowed surface node and must cover their ranges completely
The derived cache is invalidated by surface rewrite, and returned arrays are fresh snapshots while their Message objects stay shared and deep-frozen
failurePolicy: fail-closed — surface metadata and request-header/tool-error consistency are validated in `validateSessionEventData` and `validateNext` during append, so a bad event never enters the log

name: session-fork-inherited-prefix
what: `SessionStore.fork(source, boundary, childSessionId)` creates a live child from a stable prefix of a live source: the boundary must be an existing inclusive seq and must not end inside an open turn, otherwise typed `SessionForkError` codes are raised (index.ts:1196-1254, codes at 870-875). The child records `inheritedEventCount` = the copied prefix length and an `isSeeded` header, and the constructor appends a tagged `session/end-seed` marker at the inherited cut (index.ts:606-610) so a later reader can tell inherited history from live work; `ownEvents()`/`isOwnSeq()` expose the cut (index.ts:648-659).
invariants: The fork boundary is an inclusive, existing, contiguous seq and never lands inside an open turn
A seeded session's constructor seed length must equal its declared inherited prefix length, and an unseeded session's inherited count must be 0
The inherited cut is durable in the log (last tagged `session/end-seed`), not only in memory
failurePolicy: fail-closed — SessionForkError with codes SESSION_NOT_FOUND, SESSION_NOT_LIVE, SESSION_ALREADY_EXISTS, INVALID_BOUNDARY, OPEN_TURN
constants: Fork error codes: SESSION_NOT_FOUND, SESSION_NOT_LIVE, SESSION_ALREADY_EXISTS, INVALID_BOUNDARY, OPEN_TURN (packages/core/session/src/index.ts:870-875)

name: crash-repair-torn-tail-and-interrupted-turn-closers
what: Crash recovery has a physical half and a semantic half. Physically, the JSONL reader never returns a torn tail: it records `tornTruncateTo` (and, for Zstandard, the complete records recovered from a torn final frame as `recoveredTail`), and the write path truncates the torn bytes with fsync and durably rewrites recovered events before the handle's first new append (index.ts:736-739, 840-844, 1287-1296; storage.ts:328-337). Semantically, `interruptedTurnClosers(events)` synthesizes deterministic closers — error `tool/result` events for unmatched calls (codes TOOL_NOT_STARTED / TOOL_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN), then any open `step/end`, then `turn/end {reason:{kind:'interrupted'}}` — reusing the last event's timestamp; resume appends them through the write handle as an ordinary batch, and read-only observers balance a cold log in memory only.
invariants: A torn physical tail is discarded and fsynced before any new append, so duplicate seq numbers can never be written
Synthetic closers are the only crash story: an interrupted turn is closed, never resumed in place
Closer synthesis is deterministic (reuses the last event's time) and only runs for a log whose tail turn is open
failurePolicy: mixed — a torn-tail repair that fails rejects the append (fail-closed), while a balanced/empty log yields no closers and unmatched-call repair degrades into explicit error results the model can read

name: write-lease-and-lazy-materialization
what: A created session is visible to this process immediately but has no filesystem footprint: `create` registers a pending entry and returns a handle with `materialized:false`, and the session materializes on its first append or on an explicit flush (index.ts:308-327; storage.ts:203-212). Write ownership is claimed in two stages — an in-process claim at write-open (`tracker.claimWrite(id)` / `pendingOf`, index.ts:340-366) and a cross-process kernel lock acquired lazily right before the first materializing write (`ensureLease`, storage.ts:345-354). The lock is a non-blocking `flock(2)` on `session.lock` inside the session directory, or a Windows named kernel semaphore derived from that path, so a crashed holder never blocks a successor and no expiry can expropriate a live writer.
invariants: At most one active writer per session id — in-process claim plus kernel lock; readers never touch the lock
An unmaterialized session has no durable artifact, so a crash before first materialization means the session never existed
A POSIX lock names an inode, so after locking the holder must verify the locked inode is still the file at the lock path
failurePolicy: fail-closed — SessionAlreadyOwnedError on contention (EBUSY on Windows, EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK on POSIX); a failed write-open releases both the kernel lock and the in-process claim before rethrowing

name: write-behind-batching-and-flush-barrier
what: Persistence is split into a best-effort append feed and an explicit durability barrier. Published events are routed by session id into a per-handle buffer that drains through the handle's mutation chain after a bounded batching window (`LIVE_WRITE_BATCH_MAX_DELAY_MS = 200`, storage.ts:36, 274-316); a drain failure retains the batch in order and pauses the timer so a later flush can retry loudly. The barrier is `session/flush`: the backend handles it by draining the routed buffer then flushing the handle (storage.ts:534-547), `SessionStore.flush(session)` awaits every listener in parallel and rethrows the first rejection (core/session/src/index.ts:1137-1154), and the service-wide `flushAll` aggregates per-session failures into an AggregateError (storage.ts:508-523).
invariants: Only a resolved flush promises durability; a resolved append is merely accepted, ordered, and visible to later reads on the same backend instance
A failed drain must retain the buffered events in order rather than dropping or reordering them
An empty created session becomes durably listable only through flush (handle.flush materializes a header-only artifact)
failurePolicy: mixed — append is best-effort and background drain failures are logged with the buffer retained; the flush barrier is fail-closed (first listener rejection is rethrown; service-wide flush raises AggregateError)

name: semantic-checkpoint-policy
what: `session-checkpoint-policy` converts the raw flush barrier into semantic durability checkpoints by wrapping three boundaries: `llm/stream` defers adapter dispatch until `ctx.sessions.flush(session)` resolves for the complete logged request prefix (index.ts:29-38, 64-68), `tools/execute` flushes the recorded call before a top-level tool body runs (index.ts:70-75), and `agent/pre-step` flushes everything the preceding step committed (index.ts:79-82). Nested tool dispatches deliberately reuse the durable outer call.
invariants: A checkpoint rejection must prevent the downstream adapter or tool body from running
Only top-level tool dispatches checkpoint (exec.parent must be undefined)
Checkpoints happen before side effects, not after, so a crash cannot leave an unlogged side effect
failurePolicy: fail-closed at both side-effect boundaries — a rejected flush means the model call or tool body is never invoked; a tool call cancelled after the checkpoint is answered with a canonical aborted result

name: session-format-adjacent-migration-chain
what: A session log declares one monotonic logical format version (`SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION = 3`) that is bumped only for structural changes; every historical generation keeps its own physical codec and one adjacent migration edge (v0->v1, v1->v2, v2->v3). `defineSessionFormatMigration` rejects a non-adjacent edge and `CompiledSessionFormatChain` compiles the complete inventory at construction time, failing if any `vN->vN+1` step for `0..currentVersion-1` is missing, duplicated, or leads past the current version (chain.ts:24-34, 50-87); a stored version selects a precompiled contiguous slice and an unsupported/newer version produces a status or typed refusal rather than a partial read. The shipped instance is generated build-static in `session-format-catalog` with all four codecs and all three edges wired directly, so historical readability does not depend on mounted plugins.
invariants: Migration edges are adjacent, uniquely named, and complete from v0 to the build's current version — no gaps, no dynamic lookup
Both sides of every edge must agree: the chain is only valid when an older writer's codec and the edge chain are compiled together
Filenames encode the generation: version 0 is `session.jsonl`, later generations are `session.v<N>.jsonl`
failurePolicy: mixed — header classification is fail-soft (returns a `current | migration-required | unsupported | malformed` status object), while restore, encode, and every migration step are fail-closed with SessionFormatError / SessionFormatUnsupportedMigrationError
constants: catalog currentVersion = 3, codecs v0/v1/v2/v3, migrations v0->v1, v1->v2, v2->v3 (packages/session/session-format-catalog/src/generated.ts:14-18)

name: generation-migration-publication
what: A historical generation is never rewritten: migration streams the source through the adjacent chain into a staged temp file, verifies the staged file's bytes and sha256 digest in an isolated Worker Thread against the expected id and event count, re-checks the source's physical identity (`dev:ino:size:mtime:ctime`) to detect a concurrent writer, and only then publishes the new current generation with `link()` (deliberately not `rename()`, so two processes cannot clobber each other) followed by a directory fsync (generation.ts:879-938, 812-838). If the link reports EEXIST, the competing current file is validated instead — it must match the staged bytes/digest — so concurrent migrations converge on one winner. Without a current generation, a legacy `session.jsonl` is migrated and adopted rather than rewritten.
invariants: Immutable generations: migration writes a new file and never mutates the historical source
Publication is exclusive and no-clobber (link fails with EEXIST); a lost race is resolved by validating the winner, not by overwriting
Staged bytes/digest must equal the verified bytes/digest before publication and the source identity must be unchanged after verification
failurePolicy: fail-closed — digest/identity mismatch, worker failure, or a non-collision filesystem error rejects and removes the staged temp; a cleanup failure joins the primary failure in an AggregateError

name: unknown-event-vocabulary-refusal
what: The append-only log is merge-extensible, so a reader that meets an event type it does not know must refuse rather than silently skip it unless the writer marked the event `ignorable: true` (packages/core/session/src/types.ts:473-483). The build publishes its vocabulary as a generated 56-entry set `KNOWN_SESSION_EVENT_TYPES`, and `validateStoredEvents` refuses any stored event outside that set that lacks the marker, plus the one retired shape hiding under a known type (`request/header` with reason `"fallback"`), before adopting and freezing the events (session-persistence/src/storage-contract.ts:69-104). Writes are also constrained at append time by `assertSessionEventEnvelope`, which admits only the seven envelope keys.
invariants: Absent `ignorable` means required: an unknown required event must refuse the whole read, never be dropped
Vocabulary growth for purely informational records is expressed by the persisted `ignorable` marker, not by runtime event-name registration
Retired pre-release shapes under a still-known event type are refused explicitly
failurePolicy: fail-closed — SessionFormatUnsupportedError for unknown/retired vocabulary, SessionPersistenceCorruptionError for records that fail validation
constants: Envelope keys accepted by a write: type, seq, time, data, surfaceOp, sourceEventSeqs, ignorable (packages/core/session/src/index.ts:204-217)

name: projection-registry-checkpoint-restore
what: `ctx.sessionProjections` drives per-session derived state: a domain registers a unit (key, zod state schema, pure `init`/`apply`, optional wire view, `stateVersion`) and the registry folds every committed `session/event` into every registered unit, notifying the change feed only when a unit's raw view changes by `Object.is` (session-projection/src/index.ts:199-223, 233-293). The same service is the read side of the persisted cache: `checkpoint()` emits detached `(ver, seq, val)` rows, `restoreFloor()` anchors a tail read one event below the lowest usable watermark so a shrunken log is detected, and `restore()`/`viewCheckpoint()` re-seed from version-matching rows and refold the tail (index.ts:396-435, 448-509). Consumers such as `sessionStats` and `turnOutline` supply only the pure fold and register it as an effect on their own fiber.
invariants: Unit functions must be synchronous and their state must be plain JSON — the persisted-cache precondition
A row is a fold shortcut, never authority: a `ver` mismatch, a malformed value, or a watermark past the stored log end discards it and refolds
Registration is fiber-owned: unloading a domain removes its key from snapshots, and a key shared by N registrants survives until the last one unloads
failurePolicy: mixed — registration conflicts and a discarded row with `baseSeq > 0` throw (fail-closed), while malformed or mismatched rows are skipped so a cold consumer sees the key as not-yet-available (fail-soft)
constants: Each unit declares a non-negative integer `stateVersion`; a mismatched or absent row pulls the restore floor to 0 (packages/session/session-projection/src/index.ts:270-272, 425-435)

name: projection-cache-write-behind
what: `SessionProjectionCache` persists the projection registry's checkpoints into the `session_projcache` storage domain on a throttled write-behind: a dirty counter plus a timer, plus three mandatory write points — session creation, every `turn/end`, and disposal (the live-to-cold moment) (session-projection-cache/src/index.ts:301-352). Each session document binds the checkpoint rows to a log identity (format version, createdAt, cwd, isSeeded, inherited cut) so a recreated id or a swapped persistence root cannot seed state folded from an unrelated log, and the domain is declared `layout: 'per-record'` so a bad document is discarded per session rather than bricking the medium.
invariants: The cached record is derived data only: a stale or unreadable record costs a longer tail replay, never a wrong value
Every write binds the rows to the session's log identity; identity mismatch means the record reads as absent
The write path flushes the log before persisting a checkpoint, so a cache record can lag the log but never lead it
failurePolicy: fail-soft — every durable write goes through `flushSoft`, which logs a warning and leaves the cache stale, self-healing on the next write; a cold-read write-back is fire-and-forget with a logged warning
constants: domain spec: name 'session_projcache', version 7, compatibleVersions [3,4,5,6], invalidRecords 'backup-and-skip', layout 'per-record' (packages/session/session-projection-cache/src/spec.ts:98-105)
writeEveryEvents = 200 and writeIntervalMs = 5000 are required deployment config (packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml:162-166)

name: session-lifecycle-ownership
what: `SessionStore` separates construction, entry, and announcement so publication is transactional: `prepare` builds a detached session (validating id, cwd, seed continuity and header fields), `enter` installs the module-private append/publication hooks and returns a detach disposer, and `announce` emits `session/created` exactly once (core/session/src/index.ts:962-1004, 1028-1062, 1083-1111). `create` folds the three into one generator effect owned by the calling fiber, so a synchronous throwing creation listener rolls the attach back with a paired `session/disposed`; a session published outside that lifecycle persists nothing. Append/announce reentrancy is refused, and detach requested during dispatch is deferred until the dispatch unwinds.
invariants: One store entry per session id: enter re-checks for a duplicate so a stale prepared session can never displace a live one
A synchronous `session/created` throw vetoes and rolls back with a paired disposal; an async rejection only logs
Detach during an in-flight announce/append is deferred, never executed mid-dispatch
failurePolicy: fail-closed — duplicate id, already-attached, double-announce, reentrant append, and operations on a non-live session all throw; observer failures are contained per listener and logged

name: versioned-kv-storage-domain
what: Session durability sits on a two-layer storage stack: a `storage` hub with a registry of named backends (json, sqlite) and a `storage-domain` facility that opens schema-validated, change-emitting KV domains with a per-domain declaration (`name`, `version`, `compatibleVersions`, `layout`, `invalidRecords`). The JSON backend publishes whole documents atomically — same-directory temp opened `wx` at 0o600, fsync of the file, `rename()` over the target, fsync of the parent directory on POSIX — and its per-record layout treats a malformed or version-unaccepted document as foreign (reads as absent) so one bad record cannot brick a unit. The SQLite backend stamps `PRAGMA user_version` last and rejects any non-current stamped layout, and all domain writes are ordered durability -> memory -> `domain/changed` emission on a single per-domain chain.
invariants: A domain's declaration is the single source of its identity, version, layout, and record schema; validation happens at module load
Per-record reads accept only the current version plus declared compatibleVersions; any other stamp is discarded, never migrated in place
A delivered write is atomic on the medium and durable once resolved; the unit does not serialize concurrent writers — ordering is the caller's chain
failurePolicy: mixed — fail-closed for open/config/version-mismatch and whole-unit layouts; fail-soft for per-record JSON (foreign/stale/unreadable documents read as absent) and for `invalidRecords: 'backup-and-skip'` (record moved aside as `<key>.json.bak.<stamp>`, error logged, domain opens without it)
constants: JSON atomic publish: temp `.<uuid>.tmp`, open 'wx' mode 0o600, file fsync, rename, POSIX directory fsync (packages/storage/storage-json/src/atomic.ts:24-40)
per-record document shape `{version, record}` serialized with 2-space indent + trailing newline (packages/storage/storage-json/src/format.ts:97-99)

name: session-telemetry-record-capture
what: `ctx.sessionTelemetry` is a backend-agnostic record seam over the canonical log: a coordinator mirrors each committed event as one ledger record (deep copy of `data`, a redaction waterfall `session-telemetry/record`, then a non-blocking `emit`) and adds ops records for `agent-error` and shutdown, with a module-scope `handoffCursor` WeakMap advanced only when a record is handed over (session-telemetry/src/coordinator.ts:92-124, 151-162). Live capture is the default and installs listeners on session creation, disposal, event, flush and agent error; the shipped OTel backend instead uses `{capture:'on-demand', includeHistory:true}` and releases a prefix only when explicit feedback authorizes it, exporting OTel log records (not spans, not metrics) through a `LoggerProvider` + `BatchLogRecordProcessor` + OTLP/HTTP exporter with a backend-owned shutdown deadline.
invariants: Capture must never alter or rewrite the canonical session log; redaction applies to the exported copy only
A capture failure withholds exactly one record and never reaches the agent loop (per-record containment)
Only feedback authored by this session (seq >= inheritedEventCount) authorizes an OTel upload; fork-inherited feedback does not
failurePolicy: mixed — each record is contained fail-closed (a throwing listener or backend error logs and skips that record); backend shutdown rejection is caught and logged; the OTel plugin fails closed at load on invalid exporter/processor config
constants: deployment: exporter.timeoutMillis 1000, processor scheduledDelayMillis 10000, maxQueueSize 2048, maxExportBatchSize 2048, exportTimeoutMillis 1500 (packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml:188-197)

name: llm-backed-session-title
what: `ctx.sessionTitle` folds the last `session/title` event into a client-visible `title` projection (stateVersion 1) plus a host-only `titleInput` unit, and exposes a single-slot provider registry; a provider receives the eligible human messages and returns a title plus the cited `messageSeqs` (session-title/src/index.ts:263-292, 295-311). Cadence is data-driven, not timer-driven: an eligible `user/message` records a pending revision and the model call starts only once the exact request route is logged, with a revision counter plus AbortController superseding stale work. Two model providers ship: `session-title-first-prompt-llm` (registered as the base-bundle row id `session-title-llm`, automatic = first-prompt) and the opt-in `session-title-all-prompts-llm`; the shared policy package appends a log-only `session/title-llm-request` event before dispatch.
invariants: A title is durable state in the log, not mutable metadata: readers fold the latest `session/title` event
Only one provider may be registered per service; a second registration is refused
A stale revision's result must never commit — supersession is checked before the append
failurePolicy: mixed — explicit callers (`rename`, `refresh`) get fail-closed SessionTitleInvalidError and service-disposed errors, while the automatic path contains provider failures, logs a warning, and keeps the deterministic fallback title
constants: title-LLM policy (no library defaults): targetWords 5, targetCjkCharacters 10, maxInputBytes 4096, maxOutputTokens 64, timeoutMs 60000 (packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml:57-62)

name: session-controller-remote-facade
what: `SessionController` owns the generated `ctx.remote.session` namespace and is the host-side read/dispatch facade over the session domain: list, search, create, selectModel, modelCatalog, openWorkspacePath, rename, fork, prompt, attachment, updateQueue, cancel, page, follow (stream) and control (stream), plus sibling `skills` and `fileReferences` namespaces (api/session-controller/src/index.ts:121, 222-225). It never writes the log itself — reads go through `ctx.sessionQuery` (`observeSession`, `listSessions`, `traceSession`) or `ctx.sessions.get()` + `snapshotEvents()`, and history paging is message-aligned with a backward cursor (`page`, history.ts:77-111). Background activation is the promote step: after a cold snapshot is delivered, an observation is handed to the agent controller in a tracked promise whose failure is logged rather than surfaced.
invariants: No controller operation writes the session log or dispatches `session/flush`; durability stays with the agent loop and persistence backend
Every request is validated (address, page range, through-cursor) before any storage read
Cold reads must not activate an agent; activation is a separate, tracked promotion step
failurePolicy: mixed — request/address/state failures throw typed RemoteError codes (session/not-found, session/conflict, session/agent-busy, gateway/bad-request, subagent/unauthorized, ...), while background promotion failure and projection-lookup failure are logged and degrade

name: cross-session-reference-snapshot
what: `sessionReferenceResolver` injects another session's projected conversation into the live one as untrusted, read-only context: an `agent/pre-step` prepend hook parses `@[label](dsh-session:...)` mentions out of direct user messages and places each prepared snapshot immediately after the message that cited it (context/session-reference/src/index.ts:127-142, 298-355). The snapshot is read from persistence via `ctx.sessionQuery.readSurface(sessionId)` — never from a live Session object — and is budgeted: a per-source UTF-8 limit derived from the model context window (4 bytes/token heuristic) with a 64 KiB floor, oldest-first whole-message dropping, then head/tail truncation of the longest message; a truncated preview carries omission facts plus a spilled full-transcript locator when spill storage is composed.
invariants: The referenced content is untrusted and read-only: it never becomes durable history of the source session and never mutates persistence
A reference to the receiving session itself is refused, and at most MAX_REFERENCES sources are accepted per message
A preview that omits text must advertise the omission (bytes, whole messages) and locate the full transcript or state that it is unavailable
failurePolicy: fail-closed via SessionReferenceError codes (INVALID_CONFIG, INVALID_REFERENCE, SELF_REFERENCE, TOO_MANY, READ_FAILED, BUDGET_EXCEEDED, CANCELLED), with fail-soft degradation for optional spill storage (unavailable notice) and for a missing model context capacity (falls back to the default byte budget)
constants: spilled transcript fragments text at 64 Unicode code points per line (packages/context/session-reference/src/spill.ts:77)

name: deepseek-session-log-contribution
what: `session-log-deepseek` ships the canonical log suffix to the official DeepSeek API as a request field: it registers a `dsh_session_log` contribution whose value carries `version: 1`, the session format version, wire header, `afterSeq`/`throughSeq` and the events after the last accepted watermark, and its `accept` callback appends a `session-log-deepseek/delivery-accepted` event back into the canonical log (src/index.ts:157-191). The watermark is folded incrementally from those acceptance events with a WeakMap cache (`acceptedThrough`, index.ts:117-150), so restart recovery can conservatively resend an uncertain tail without a second store. The plugin is registered in production compositions but `enabled` defaults to false, and no shipped bundle row sets it, so the contribution is inert there.
invariants: The acceptance watermark lives in the canonical log; no separate delivery store exists
A delivery-accepted event must name this session, reference an earlier seq, and carry a well-formed format version — otherwise it is a malformed log
Unaccepted suffixes are resent; accepted prefixes are never re-sent
failurePolicy: fail-closed on read (throws on a missing event below the captured length, a malformed acceptance format version, or a malformed watermark), with degrade-to-undefined when the request has no session id or the session is not live

name: append-only-rollout-with-compacted-projection
what: Durable session state is an append-only JSONL rollout. `RolloutRecorder` owns a `tokio::mpsc` command channel to a background writer task (`AddItems`, `Persist`, `Flush`, `Shutdown` all carry oneshot acks), and the writer task's terminal IO failure is retained in a `Mutex<Option<Arc<IoError>>>` so a dead writer is observable rather than silently swallowing writes. Which items reach the file is decided by `is_persisted_rollout_item`: compaction, turn-context, world-state, security-score and session-meta markers are always persisted, `ItemCompleted` only in Paginated history mode, legacy message events only in Legacy mode, and transient events (deltas, begin/end tool events, warnings, guardian assessments, approvals) never. Compaction does not rewrite the file — it appends a `RolloutItem::Compacted` carrying `replacement_history`, and replay replaces the accumulated history with it, so the model-visible history is a projection over an unchanged log.
invariants: The rollout file is append-only; a compaction checkpoint must be appended, never used to rewrite prior lines (core/src/session/mod.rs:3391-3392 persists only `RolloutItem::Compacted`).
The world-state baseline must be persisted *after* the replacement history that established it (core/src/session/mod.rs:3393-3397).
Transient events must stay out of the rollout — `should_persist_event_msg` ends in an explicit `=> false` arm covering deltas, approvals, warnings and begin events (rollout/src/policy.rs:122-183).
failurePolicy: fail-soft
constants: Filename shape `rollout-<timestamp>-<conversation_id>.jsonl`, with an optional `_<rollout_id>` suffix when `thread/revert` keeps the thread id but starts a new immutable rollout (rollout/src/recorder.rs:99-104)

name: rollout-reconstruction-on-resume
what: Resuming rebuilds the model-visible history by replaying a suffix of rollout items into a fresh `ContextManager`. A reverse scan stops at the newest `Compacted` item that carries a `replacement_history`, so the suffix starts from that checkpoint; the base replacement history is installed first and the suffix items are then replayed, with `InterAgentCommunication` items converted to model input and `ThreadRolledBack` events calling `history.drop_last_n_user_turns(n)`. Legacy compaction items with `replacement_history: None` take a second path: `collect_annotated_user_messages` plus `build_compacted_history` rebuild the summary, and the reference context item is deliberately cleared — the source notes this produces a temporary out-of-distribution prompt shape. `EventMsg`, `TurnContext`, `WorldState`, `SecurityRiskScore` and `SessionMeta` items contribute nothing to history reconstruction.
invariants: The reverse scan must stop before any compaction carrying a replacement history, so the loop's `Some(replacement_history)` branch is documented unreachable and exists only as defence (core/src/session/rollout_reconstruction.rs:345-348).
A legacy compaction without replacement history must clear the reference context item rather than guess one (core/src/session/rollout_reconstruction.rs:386-389).
`ThreadRolledBack` must be applied as a user-turn drop during replay, since it is a durable history mutation event (core/src/session/rollout_reconstruction.rs:369-371).
failurePolicy: fail-soft
constants: fallback_window_number is derived by counting Compacted items, saturating to u64::MAX (core/src/session/rollout_reconstruction.rs:312-318)

name: six-database-sqlite-state-runtime
what: Durable non-transcript state lives in six separate SQLite files under the sqlite home (`state_5`, `logs_2`, `goals_1`, `memories_1`, `queue_1`, `thread_history_1`), each declared as a `RuntimeDbSpec` with its own sqlx `Migrator` compiled from a checked-in migrations directory (51 state migrations plus separate logs/goals/memories/queue/thread-history sets). Connections are opened with WAL journal mode and a 5 s busy timeout. `repair_legacy_recency_migration_version` hand-repairs the `_sqlx_migrations` row for version 39 only when the migration table exists, the checksum matches and the version is absent — an explicit compatibility shim for a previously shipped migration. A read-only single-connection pool exists for audit paths that must not migrate or repair.
invariants: Migrations must stay one directory per database; the migrators are compiled with `sqlx::migrate!` over distinct folders so a schema change cannot land in the wrong DB (state/src/migrations.rs:6-11).
The legacy repair must be a no-op unless the stored checksum equals the embedded one — it must never force-insert a migration row it did not verify (state/src/migrations.rs:56-118).
Known-but-newer migration versions are ignored, not rejected, so a downgraded binary still opens the DB (state/src/migrations.rs:16-21).
failurePolicy: fail-closed
constants: STATE_DB_FILENAME = state_5.sqlite, LOGS_DB_FILENAME = logs_2.sqlite, GOALS_DB_FILENAME = goals_1.sqlite, MEMORIES_DB_FILENAME = memories_1.sqlite, QUEUE_DB_FILENAME = queue_1.sqlite, THREAD_HISTORY_DB_FILENAME = thread_history_1.sqlite (state/src/sqlite.rs:29-34)
50 state migrations + 2 queue + 4 thread_history + 2 goals + 1 memory + 2 logs (state/*_migrations/)

name: rollout-lineage-and-compression
what: Long-lived sessions are compacted on disk: `rollout/src/compression.rs` gz/zstd-compresses finished rollout files behind a run marker so only one compressor runs at a time, and lineage resolution walks `SessionMeta.history_base` pointers to assemble an ordered `RolloutLineage` of bounded segments, detecting cycles and coordinating with the writer lock while a referenced compressed segment is materialized. A `RolloutReferenceIndex` scans active and archived session directories keyed by immutable rollout id and computes inverse reference counts, with a deadline variant that returns no partial index.
invariants: Lineage resolution must fail closed on a repeated rollout id rather than loop (thread-store/src/local/rollout_lineage.rs:92-94).
A reference-index scan past its deadline returns None, never a truncated index (rollout/src/rollout_reference_index.rs:48-64).
A rollout's own history_base equal to its own id is not a reference (rollout/src/rollout_reference_index.rs:146-156).
failurePolicy: mixed
constants: compression::WORKER_MAX_RUNTIME = 5 h, RUN_MARKER_STALE_AFTER = 6 h, COMPRESSION_LEVEL = 3, COMPRESSED_SUFFIX = .zst, RUN_MARKER_FILE_NAME = rollout-compression.lock (rollout/src/compression.rs:24-31, :183-186)

name: durable-queued-user-submissions
what: `codex queue --thread <id> --message <text>` does not write to the in-memory input queue; it persists a row into the `queued_items` SQLite table (id PK, thread_id, payload_json, queue_order with UNIQUE(thread_id, queue_order)) behind the storage-neutral `QueueStore` trait. `QueuedItemService` drains items one at a time into an idle thread and deletes each only after the submission reports `StartIfIdleSubmission::Started`, so a rejected start leaves the item queued. A background `watch_external_messages` task ticks every 10 s, checks SQLite's inexpensive data version, then uses the `queued_thread_revisions` table (maintained by AFTER INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE triggers) to find only changed threads and spawns an independent per-thread dispatch task, so one blocked thread cannot starve the others. Item count is capped per thread.
invariants: FIFO per thread is load-bearing: dispatch always reads page size 1 from offset 0 and deletes only on a Started submission (ext/queue/src/service.rs:226-236).
The per-thread cap MAX_QUEUE_ITEMS = 100 must be enforced at enqueue (state/src/lib.rs:94).
Revision bookkeeping must be trigger-maintained so external writers are seen without polling the items table (state/queue_migrations/0002_queued_thread_revisions.sql:9-34).
failurePolicy: fail-soft
constants: watch_external_messages interval = 10 s; per-thread dispatch retry sleep = 10 s (ext/queue/src/service.rs:88-95, :238)
Only user-message input may be enqueued; QueueServiceError::InvalidInput otherwise (ext/queue/src/service.rs:56-61)

name: global-message-history-jsonl
what: A separate global append-only `~/.codex/history.jsonl` records one JSON object per line (`{session_id, ts, text}`) for every user message, independent of the per-session rollout. The module documents the write contract explicitly: prepare the full line including the trailing newline and write it in a single `write(2)` with the descriptor opened `O_APPEND`, relying on the POSIX guarantee that writes up to `PIPE_BUF` are atomic, so concurrent processes cannot interleave partial records. Reads use buffered line iteration.
invariants: A record must be written as one full line in one `write(2)` with O_APPEND — splitting the record across writes breaks the atomicity the concurrency story depends on (message-history/src/lib.rs:11-15).
The record schema is fixed at {session_id, ts, text}; appending a field requires a reader-side story because the file is never rewritten (message-history/src/lib.rs:6-9).
failurePolicy: fail-soft

name: filesystem-probed-journal-mode-with-per-host-db
what: This crate is not an event log - it contains no append API, no event rows and no crash repair. It is a filesystem-aware `PRAGMA journal_mode` selector plus a per-host database path derivation. `JournalMode::for_db_path` classifies the database's parent directory through `is_network_fs` and returns `Wal` on a local filesystem or `Truncate` on a network one (xai-sqlite-journal/src/lib.rs:43-82); `Truncate.effective_db_path` then rewrites the filename to a per-host sibling (`worktrees.db` -> `worktrees.h-<host>.db`) using a lowercased-alphanumeric hostname discriminator capped at 24 characters (lib.rs:108-133). `apply` orders `locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE` -> `journal_mode=TRUNCATE` -> `locking_mode=NORMAL` so converting an already-WAL-stamped database never mmaps a `-shm` file (lib.rs:199-209). The module doc gives the concrete failure being avoided: WAL keeps its wal-index in an mmap'd `-shm`, and when `$HOME` is NFS-mounted a peer host truncating or rebuilding that file during recovery rips the mapping out and the next wal-index read dies with SIGBUS (lib.rs:1-13). The read-only open on the Truncate arm deliberately opens READ_WRITE without CREATE and then sets `query_only=true`, because POSIX forbids write-locking an O_RDONLY file descriptor (lib.rs:151-183). The network magic list covers NFS/SMB/SMB2/CIFS/9p/CODA/AFS/kAFS/CEPH/Lustre/GFS2/GPFS/OCFS2/WekaFS/FUSE (lib.rs:353-376); on macOS the authoritative signal is the absence of `MNT_LOCAL` (lib.rs:401-411); on Windows it probes UNC prefixes and `GetDriveTypeW == DRIVE_REMOTE` (lib.rs:478-513). Five consumers are wired: xai-fast-worktree, xai-grok-dashboard-store, xai-grok-foreign-sessions, xai-grok-memory and xai-grok-session-search.
invariants: Callers must create the parent directory before calling `for_db_path`, because classification reads the directory and the DB file may not exist yet.
Per-host suffixing must stay idempotent, or a sidecar file operation would re-suffix an already-resolved path.
WAL must never be selected for a database on a network filesystem; the per-host path is what makes that hold even against an old binary that stamps WAL.
Converting a WAL-stamped DB to TRUNCATE must go through EXCLUSIVE locking before the journal_mode change and back to NORMAL after.
`apply` must set `busy_timeout` first or go through `apply_with_retry`, because lock paths only partially honor the busy handler.
failurePolicy: mixed - detection fails OPEN to WAL (`is_network_fs` returns false on any statfs error), the env kill-switch fails loud-but-open (an invalid value warns and falls through to detection), and mode application fails CLOSED after a bounded retry whose error is re-wrapped with the elapsed time.

constants.name: RETRY_PAUSE
constants.value: 20 ms, with a per-attempt busy clamp of 20 ms..1000 ms

name: pid-liveness-active-session-registry-with-atomic-replace
what: Open sessions are tracked in `~/.grok/active_sessions.json` so an unclean exit is detectable rather than invisible, and every mutation is a locked read-modify-write. `with_locked_state` takes a blocking exclusive `fs2` lock on `active_sessions.lock`, reads the JSON array, applies a closure, then atomically replaces the file via write-temp plus `fs::rename`, cleaning the temp file up if the rename fails (xai-grok-active-sessions/src/lib.rs:81-130). A separate `try_with_locked_state` uses `try_lock_exclusive` so a signal handler never blocks (lib.rs:141-158). `collect_crashed_in` partitions entries on `is_pid_alive` and returns only the dead ones (lib.rs:173-204); on unix an EPERM probe counts as alive (lib.rs:184).
invariants: Every write must go through the tempfile-plus-rename path, or a crash mid-write truncates the registry.
A `try_unregister` that returns false on contention must leave the entry intact for next-launch reaping - it does, because the closure never runs.
The blocking and non-blocking variants must share one `locked_mutate`, so their semantics cannot drift apart.
PID-liveness is the only liveness signal, so a recycled PID can make a crashed session look live; the design accepts this and reports only dead-PID orphans.
failurePolicy: mixed - the registry read is fail-open (a missing file, an empty file, or corrupt JSON all yield an empty list, with a warning only for corruption), IO errors other than NotFound propagate, lock contention in the non-blocking path is a soft `Ok(false)`/`Ok(None)`, and PID probing degrades to 'assume alive' on unsupported platforms.

name: epoch-versioned-single-flight-gateway-catalog
what: A gateway tool catalog is fetched behind a single-flight gate that cannot resurrect a disabled catalog. `ManagedMcpState` keeps a `gateway_tool_epoch` that is bumped by `enable`/`disable`, and `complete_gateway_tool_fetch(epoch, ..)` commits the fetched catalog only if the epoch still matches, so a fetch that was in flight when the catalog was disabled is discarded rather than applied (xai-grok-shell-session-support/src/managed_mcp.rs:43-87, :304-355). `get_or_fetch_gateway_tool_catalog` single-flights waiters on a `tokio::sync::Notify` and rolls the state back to `NotFetched` on failure, so a later caller retries instead of inheriting a poisoned result. An `Err` is deliberately distinct from `Ok(empty_catalog)` - a failed fetch and an genuinely empty catalog are different states (managed_mcp.rs:131).
invariants: A completed fetch must be epoch-checked before commit; without it a stale in-flight response silently re-enables a disabled catalog.
The epoch is bumped on both enable and disable, so the check does not assume the direction of the change.
Failure must roll back to `NotFetched` rather than caching the error, or one transient failure would permanently deny the catalog.
`Err` and `Ok(empty)` must stay distinguishable at the API boundary.
failurePolicy: fail-soft with an explicit distinction - a failed fetch does not populate the cache and does not read as an empty catalog; waiters are released through a Notify rather than polling.

name: dashboard-capacity-eviction-with-schema-gate
what: The dashboard workspace store enforces a hard capacity inside one immediate transaction and refuses rather than silently dropping pinned rows. `insert_member_inner` runs a single IMMEDIATE transaction that, at capacity, evicts `count - (capacity - 1)` least-recently-changed UNPINNED rows ordered by `last_change_unix_ms, session_id, kind`; if no row is unpinned it returns `StoreError::AllPinned` having written nothing (xai-grok-dashboard-store/src/store.rs:212-248). A newer on-disk `PRAGMA user_version` short-circuits to `open_newer_schema` with `PRAGMA query_only=true`, so an older binary reads a newer store read-only instead of corrupting it (store_open.rs:97). The store states an ownership contract in its own doc: it owns every byte of that SQL, consumers get only the typed API, and every statement names its columns so decode indexes never depend on table order (xai-grok-dashboard-store/src/lib.rs:1-14).
invariants: Eviction and insert must be one transaction, or a failed insert can leave rows evicted.
Pinned rows are never evicted; if only pinned rows remain the operation fails with `AllPinned` and writes nothing rather than exceeding capacity.
A newer schema must be opened read-only through `query_only`, never migrated downward.
Columns are named explicitly in every statement so additive schema evolution cannot clobber a column an older binary does not know about.
failurePolicy: fail-closed on capacity (refuse with `AllPinned` rather than violate the bound) and fail-safe on schema version (read-only open instead of a downgrade).

name: append-only-jsonl-session-event-log
what: Each session writes an append-only `events.jsonl` of typed events, and in this tree nothing reads it back. `EventWriter::open` uses `create(true).append(true)` and, on an open failure, warns once and stores a `None` file slot so a writer is always constructible; clones share one `Arc<EventWriterInner>` holding `Mutex<Option<File>>`, making the writer `Clone + Send + Sync` for background tasks (xai-grok-session-events/src/log.rs:34-51). Each line is an RFC3339 millisecond UTC timestamp flattened with the internally-tagged `Event` (log.rs:62-81).
invariants: `emit` must never panic and must not propagate: it returns unit and drops the line on a serialization or lock failure.
The write-error warning stays behind an `error_logged` swap so a broken disk cannot log once per event.
`EventWriter::noop()` must be indistinguishable from a working writer to callers - it pre-sets the latch so it never warns.
failurePolicy: fail-open and silent by design - an open failure, a poisoned mutex and a serialization failure all return without emitting.

name: bounded-metadata-only-foreign-session-scan
what: Other coding agents' session stores are read as metadata with hard caps, not ingested. The module doc describes the shape as a bounded, metadata-only listing (xai-grok-foreign-sessions/src/lib.rs:1-6), and the bounds are declared constants: at most 50 sessions per tool, a maximum session age of 30 days, a 200-character title cap, and a 5-minute tolerance for timestamps that appear to come from the future (lib.rs:20-23). The public surface is narrow - a full scan and a `most_recent_foreign_session` convenience - so the caller gets a listing and not a parser for foreign formats.
invariants: Metadata only: the caps make it structurally impossible for a foreign store to pull unbounded content into this process.
MAX_FUTURE_SKEW exists because a clock skew between agents must not let a session be treated as recent indefinitely.
The title is truncated, so a hostile or pathological foreign title cannot blow up display or index sizes.
failurePolicy: fail-soft - bounded listing degrades to fewer rows; a foreign store that cannot be read contributes nothing rather than failing the caller.

name: jsonl-transcript-append-log
what: A session is an append-only JSONL file at <configHome>/projects/<sanitized-project>/<sessionId>.jsonl written with mode 0o600 (src/utils/sessionStorage.ts:194-206, 505-513). Only user, assistant, attachment and system entries are transcript messages; progress entries are explicitly excluded because including them caused chain forks that orphaned real messages on resume (sessionStorage.ts:124-142). The transcript is the event log the resume path, hooks (transcript_path) and the SDK all read, and it is addressed through sessionProjectDir rather than the live cwd so a resumed or branched session does not drift into a second file (sessionStorage.ts:203-214).
invariants: progress/ephemeral entries must never be written into the parentUuid chain
every transcript file is created 0o600 inside a 0o700 project directory
the transcript path is derived from sessionId plus sessionProjectDir, never from the current cwd alone
failurePolicy: fail-closed on write errors: appendToFile retries once after mkdir and then logs and rethrows rather than silently dropping transcript data (sessionStorage.ts:505-526)

name: parent-uuid-conversation-chain
what: Each transcript entry carries a uuid and a parentUuid, so the conversation is a linked chain rather than a flat array; the write path assigns parentUuid only from chain participants (src/utils/sessionStorage.ts:144-152). Legacy transcripts that already contain progress entries are repaired at load time by bridging the chain across them (sessionStorage.ts:160-174), and deserialization filters unresolved tool uses, orphaned thinking-only assistant messages and whitespace-only assistant messages before the chain is handed back (src/utils/conversationRecovery.ts:150-194). Resume also strips permissionMode values that are not in the current PERMISSION_MODES set, because the field is unvalidated JSON from a possibly different build (conversationRecovery.ts:169-180).
invariants: a chain participant is anything that is not a progress entry
no unresolved tool_use may survive deserialization
permissionMode read from disk is validated against the current mode enum before use
failurePolicy: fail-soft: legacy progress entries are bridged rather than rejected, and unknown permission modes are dropped rather than failing the resume

name: buffered-transcript-write-pipeline
what: Transcript writes are queued per file and drained on a 100 ms timer, batching entries into newline-joined chunks and flushing early when a chunk would reach 100 MB (src/utils/sessionStorage.ts:427-428, 482-502, 528-549). The drain resolves each queued entry's promise even when the underlying append fails, so a caller can never hang on a dead filesystem; individual write errors are logged and a drain that arrives while another drain is active schedules itself again rather than racing (sessionStorage.ts:482-502).
invariants: one drain at a time per write pipeline
queued entry promises are always settled, success or failure
chunk size is bounded so a single flush cannot build an unbounded string
failurePolicy: fail-soft: a failed append is logged as an error, the batch's promises still resolve, and the remaining queue is rescheduled

name: tombstone-rewrite-guard
what: Removing an already-written message (a tombstone, used when a message is orphaned) normally rewrites the session file in place, first trying a fast 64 KB-tail path and falling back to a full read-modify-write that drops the matching uuid line (src/utils/sessionStorage.ts:812-841). Because session files can grow to multiple GB, the full rewrite is refused above a hard 50 MB cap and the tombstone is skipped with a warning instead, preventing an OOM (sessionStorage.ts:117-119, 821-829). Malformed lines are preserved verbatim rather than dropped, so a partial rewrite cannot destroy unrelated data (sessionStorage.ts:831-839).
invariants: the full-file rewrite path must be size-capped
unparseable lines are kept, never silently discarded
the tail fast-path is attempted before any full read
failurePolicy: fail-soft: an oversized file skips tombstone removal and logs a warning; the session continues with the message still present

name: session-pid-registry-and-reaper
what: Every top-level session (interactive, SDK, bg, daemon) writes a PID record to <configHome>/sessions/<pid>.json containing pid, sessionId, cwd, startedAt, kind and entrypoint, and registers an exit cleanup that unlinks it; teammates and subagents are deliberately excluded so swarm usage does not pollute the concurrency count (src/utils/concurrentSessions.ts:48-106). The PID file follows a session switch through onSessionSwitch so `claude ps` never reads the wrong transcript (concurrentSessions.ts:95-100). countConcurrentSessions filters strictly on /^\d+\.json$/, counts live PIDs and sweeps stale files, but skips sweeping on WSL where a Windows PID is not probeable (concurrentSessions.ts:148-184).
invariants: only top-level sessions register (getAgentId() != null returns false)
the PID filename matches ^\d+\.json$ before any parseInt, so notes files are never swept as stale
the sessions directory is created 0o700 and the PID file follows session switches
failurePolicy: fail-soft: registration errors are logged and return false; countConcurrentSessions returns 0 on a readdir failure

name: config-migration-ladder
what: User configuration is migrated by a version-gated sequence rather than by schema evolution: runMigrations compares getGlobalConfig().migrationVersion against CURRENT_MIGRATION_VERSION (11) and, on mismatch, runs seven idempotent migrations that rewrite settings.json (bypassPermissions-accepted, enableAllProjectMcpServers, Sonnet 1M to 4.5, legacy Opus, Opus to Opus-1M), then stamps the new version in a single saveGlobalConfig (src/main.tsx:280-301). Each migration is self-guarding: migrateOpusToOpus1m returns immediately unless the merge experiment is on and userSettings.model is exactly 'opus', and writes the new value only when it differs from the default (src/migrations/migrateOpusToOpus1m.ts:24-43). One migration is additionally gated on feature('TRANSCRIPT_CLASSIFIER') and one on the always-false bundler literal, so those two cannot run in this build (main.tsx:290-295).
invariants: every migration must be idempotent and re-runnable
the version stamp is written once, in the same pass, after all migrations
migrations mutate user settings, never the transcript
failurePolicy: fail-soft: migrations are synchronous best-effort writes; a migration that finds nothing to change returns without touching disk

name: file-checkpoint-snapshot-and-rewind
what: Before a file is edited, fileHistoryTrackEdit snapshots its pre-edit contents into a rolling per-message snapshot list of at most 100 entries keyed by message id, with each tracked path mapped to a versioned backup name (null meaning the file did not exist at that version) (src/utils/fileHistory.ts:32-55, 81-109). Restore and diff entry points (fileHistoryRewind, fileHistoryCanRestore, fileHistoryGetDiffStats, checkOriginFileChanged) let the user rewind tracked files to the state at a chosen message. Checkpointing is on by default interactively and off for SDK sessions unless CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_SDK_FILE_CHECKPOINTING is set, and either path can be disabled by env or config (fileHistory.ts:64-79).
invariants: the backup must be captured before the edit, so the pre-edit content is recoverable
at most MAX_SNAPSHOTS snapshots are retained (oldest evicted, sequence counter still increments)
a null backup name means 'file absent at this version' and must not be confused with a backup file
failurePolicy: fail-soft: with checkpointing disabled the tracking functions return immediately and edits proceed without backups

name: durable-event-log
what: EventV2 is the append-only durable log. publish() with a durable definition computes the aggregate's next sequence and writes the row inside a transaction, committing the local projection inside the same transaction via PublishOptions.commit; divergent or duplicate sequences are rejected with explicit errors ('Replay diverged at aggregate ... sequence', 'Event ... already exists at aggregate ... sequence'). replay/replayAll re-apply serialized events, and durable(aggregateID, after) returns a stream that reads the log then tails a per-aggregate wake PubSub.
invariants: A durable event's sequence must be assigned by the log, never by the caller.
A local commit hook requires a durable event (publishing a non-durable event with commit is a defect).
failurePolicy: fail-closed - duplicate or divergent sequences abort the transaction and defect; subscribers of a bounded stream are failed with SubscriberOverflowError rather than silently missing events.
constants: projector subscriber capacity used by the SSE bridge = 256 (packages/server/src/handlers/event.ts:9)
SessionRepair replays at most 10_000 events (fork; see forkDeltas)

name: session-projection-tables
what: Projections are rebuilt from events by SessionProjector: a projector decodes the event payload, dies when a durable session event lacks its aggregate sequence, and upserts the projection row; SessionAlreadyProjected marks events already applied. SessionMessageUpdater.update(adapter, event) is the message/part projection path shared by the database adapter and an in-memory adapter used by tests.
invariants: A durable Session event MUST carry the aggregate sequence; a projector must die rather than write an unsequenced row.
Projection must be idempotent - re-applying an already projected event is detected, not duplicated.
failurePolicy: fail-closed - missing aggregate sequence is a defect (Effect.die); decode failures are surfaced as typed MessageDecodeError/ContextSnapshotDecodeError to the runner.

name: session-sql-schema
what: The session store is Drizzle-over-SQLite with tables session, message, part, todo, session_message, session_input and session_context_epoch. session carries project/workspace/parent foreign keys, cost and five token counters, revert JSON, share_url, and a permission JSON column typed as PermissionV1.Ruleset. Ordering indexes (session_message_session_seq_idx unique, session_input_session_admitted_seq_idx unique, part_message_id_id_idx) make the event and input sequences enforceable at the database level.
invariants: session_message (session_id, seq) must stay unique - replay relies on it.
session_input admitted_seq/promoted_seq uniqueness must stay enforced; promotion order is derived from them.
failurePolicy: fail-closed - constraint violations abort the write; schema access errors are lifted with Effect.orDie at the call sites.

name: context-epoch-persistence
what: The system-context baseline is durable per session in session_context_epoch (baseline text, source snapshot JSON, baseline_seq). SessionContextEpoch.initialize writes the first generation; prepare() decodes the stored snapshot, and if a compaction is newer than the stored baseline it attempts SystemContext.replace, otherwise reconcile; Unchanged/ReplacementBlocked keep the stored baseline, ReplacementReady rewrites baseline+snapshot at a new sequence, and a plain update publishes SessionEvent.ContextUpdated with the delta text and advances only the snapshot.
invariants: The stored baseline_seq is the sequence at which the baseline text was materialized; it may only move forward.
A replacement must be refused (ReplacementBlocked) while an admitted source is unavailable instead of writing a partial baseline.
failurePolicy: fail-closed - an undecodable stored snapshot fails with ContextSnapshotDecodeError, and a missing epoch row during update dies ('Context Epoch not found').

name: input-admission-and-steering
what: User input enters through SessionInput.admit, which records a delivery mode of 'steer' or 'queue' and an admitted_seq from the published event; the row keeps promoted_seq null until the runner consumes it. promoteSteers(cutoff) promotes every steer delivery with admitted_seq <= cutoff and promoteNextQueued takes the oldest queued row, both strictly in admitted_seq order; hasPending(delivery) answers whether un-promoted input of a delivery kind exists.
invariants: Promotion order is admitted_seq order; promotion must be expressed as a conditional update on promoted_seq IS NULL so a row is promoted once.
Steering input is bounded by the cutoff sequence and cannot be promoted beyond it.
failurePolicy: fail-closed - projectPrompted dies with a LifecycleConflict if the projection does not match, so a divergent promotion aborts instead of duplicating input.

name: session-lifecycle-and-forking
what: Session.Service owns lifecycle: createNext builds a row with a generated slug, parent_id, default titles ('New session - ' / 'Child session - '), model and permission; create wires config-derived permission; fork copies a session up to a message id remapping message ids through an id map; children(parentID) lists direct children; remove deletes the session and recursively removes its children, tolerating broken sessions; touch updates the timestamp; setPermission/setShare/setRevert/setArchived mutate individual columns.
invariants: Removing a session must recursively remove its children.
Child sessions must carry parent_id, because delegation depth and cancellation cascade are derived from it.
failurePolicy: fail-soft - remove logs 'failed to remove session' and continues if part of the cascade fails, so one broken child cannot block deletion of the parent.

name: conversation-revert-and-snapshot
what: SessionRevert.revert records a revert point {messageID, partID, snapshot, diff} on the session, restores the snapshot recorded by a previous revert if present, applies the reverse patches for the reverted messages, and stores the resulting diff; unrevert restores the snapshot and clears the revert; cleanup (called at the start of every prompt) deletes the messages and parts after the revert point so the model never sees reverted history. Snapshot tracking is git-backed with its own git dir under global data.
invariants: Every prompt must run revert.cleanup before creating the user message, otherwise reverted content would re-enter the model context.
A revert must record the pre-revert snapshot so unrevert is possible.
failurePolicy: fail-closed - revert/unrevert require a non-busy session (Session.BusyError); snapshot restore failures are logged and the operation continues.
constants: snapshot skips files larger than 2 MiB (packages/opencode/src/snapshot/index.ts:24)

name: todo-durable-store
what: Session todos are persisted rows, not message content: Todo.update replaces the session's rows inside one transaction (delete then insert with position = array index) and then publishes Event.Updated; get reads rows ordered by position. The todowrite tool is the only writer and is deny-by-default for subagents.
invariants: The replacement must be transactional - readers must never observe a partial todo list.
position is the ordering key and part of the primary key.
failurePolicy: fail-closed - transaction errors are lifted with Effect.orDie; the event is published only after the transaction commits.

name: session-command-durable-admission
what: Prompt submission is a durable, conflict-checked command protocol. SessionCommand.admit takes an optional id (idempotency key), the prompt, a delivery mode, an intent and an expectedActiveAttemptID, and fails with PromptConflictError when the same message id already exists with a different prompt, with ActiveAttemptConflictError when the caller's expected attempt is not the active one, and with TurnConflictError on turn-level conflicts. It also owns create/restore (RestoreConflictError), switchAgent/switchModel, synthetic admission and plan-path resolution.
invariants: Re-admitting the same message id with an equivalent prompt must be idempotent and return the existing admission (SessionInput.equivalent), while a divergent prompt must fail.
An expected-active-attempt guard must be honoured so a stale caller cannot inject input into a superseded attempt.
failurePolicy: fail-closed - conflicts are typed errors and no partial admission is written.

name: durable-task-submission-protocol
what: Subagent delegation is expressed as a task_submission row keyed by the parent identity (parent session, assistant message, tool call id) plus child session, child input id, description, prompt, agent, agentPath, model, completion delivery mode ('tool' | 'parent'), status accepted/running/completed/error/cancelled/recovery-required, outcome, result message/text and error. InvocationConflict rejects a second submission for the same parent tool call, and the API exposes claim/terminalize/recovery operations.
invariants: One submission per (parentSession, assistantMessage, toolCallID) - a duplicate invocation must conflict rather than fork a second child.
A submission must terminate with an outcome; ambiguous post-crash state becomes 'recovery-required', never silently completed.
failurePolicy: fail-closed - InvocationConflict/Missing/Cancelled are typed errors; outcome includes recovery-required for the ambiguous case.
constants: statuses = accepted | running | completed | error | cancelled | recovery-required (packages/core/src/session/task-submission.ts:56)

name: task-notification-outbox
what: Completion notifications are durable: task_notification_outbox is the source of truth, a process-local PubSub sliding signal is only an advisory wakeup, and drain() is single-flight behind a Semaphore(1). Notification payloads carry {taskID, state, description, text} with state completed/error/cancelled/recovery-required, and the resulting message id is derived deterministically from the submission id (msg_task_notification_<sha256 prefix>) so re-delivery is idempotent.
invariants: The outbox, not the in-process signal, is the durable source of truth; a lost signal must not lose a notification.
The notification message id must be a pure function of the submission id.
Only one drain may run at a time.
failurePolicy: fail-soft with a durable backstop - a missed wakeup leaves the row in the outbox for the next drain.
constants: notification states = completed | error | cancelled | recovery-required (packages/core/src/session/task-notification.ts:14)

name: task-cancellation-tree
what: TaskCancellation.cancelTree cancels a whole delegation tree by ownership root: in one transaction it flips task submissions to cancelled, terminalizes the outbox rows, marks cancellation rows terminal, appends cancellation text, and abandons attempts still in started/responding/retrying/continuation. After the transaction commits it signals the notification outbox and then interrupts and waits for every affected session.
invariants: The database state must be settled inside one transaction before any session is interrupted.
Every session named by the cancellation must be interrupted and waited for, so no orphan turn keeps running.
failurePolicy: fail-closed - cancellation is recorded durably with message 'Task cancelled by ownership root'; a missing session is a typed Missing error.

name: session-projection-repair
what: SessionRepair.repairSession replays a session's durable event log (readAggregate with limit 10_000 and the SessionDurable manifest) and rebuilds missing or divergent projection rows: it repairs the attempt row when the last ProviderAttempt.Started id does not match the stored row, replaying Started/ResponseStarted/Ended/Recovery.Decided/Retried in log order so the row settles into its terminal status, and rebuilds session_input rows only for PromptAdmitted events whose row is MISSING (because projectAdmitted dies with LifecycleConflict on an existing row).
invariants: Repair must never replay an input row that already exists - only missing rows may be projected.
Attempt repair must replay ALL attempt transitions in log order, not just Started, or an ended attempt would be resurrected as started.
failurePolicy: fail-soft - repair returns {repaired: boolean} rather than failing the session; a rebuilt input row without promoted_seq is an accepted limitation documented in the module.

name: durable-session-schema
what: The fork's session schema keeps session, todo, session_message, session_input and session_context_epoch and adds durable coordination tables: task_submission, task_notification_outbox, session_cancellation, session_attempt, session_turn, session_execution, session_tool_discovery_call and session_tool_discovery. session.permission now stores PermissionV2.Ruleset and session.engine fixes the execution engine; session_execution stores the kernel generation/lease/state.
invariants: session.permission must hold the V2 rule shape {action, resource, effect}.
Kernel-only tables must never be touched by classic sessions.
failurePolicy: fail-closed - schema writes are transactional; constraint violations abort.

name: legacy-transcript-retirement-migration
what: A two-step migration chain retired the legacy transcript tables: first a session_message_tombstone table was introduced, then a later migration drops the message and part tables together with their indexes (message_session_time_created_id_idx, part_message_id_id_idx, part_session_idx) and drops the tombstone table itself. Messages now live exclusively in session_message.
invariants: The drop migration must remove the dependent indexes before dropping the tables.
After this migration no code path may read message/part.
failurePolicy: fail-closed - migrations run in a transaction; a failure aborts the migration.

name: session-lifecycle-settlement
what: SessionLifecycle settles durable state that a crashed or aborted turn left open: settleAssistant fails pending/running tool parts and the step, settleCompletedAttempt ends the provider attempt once no tool part is pending/running, terminateAttempt ends an attempt in started/responding/retrying/continuation with a terminal outcome, abandonOrphan abandons an attempt with no owner, reconcileForStart ends attempts already terminal, and endOpenTurn closes an open turn.
invariants: Settlement must publish the durable Ended events, not simply edit rows, so projections and repair agree.
Settlement must be idempotent - an already-ended attempt/turn returns false instead of double-writing.
failurePolicy: fail-closed - a terminal attempt is left terminal; settlement only ever moves state forward.

name: session-input-promotion-and-startup-candidates
what: Input admission is richer than upstream: rows carry delivery (steer|queue), an intent, and an optional synthetic descriptor with a scope, and expose pending/findForSession/hasPending, isTurnScoped/isSessionScoped, waitForPending, latestPromoted, promotedUnterminalizedAtOrBefore, cancelPending and promote/promoteSteers/promoteNextQueued. startupCandidates lists steer-delivery input rows that must be re-driven after a restart.
invariants: Synthetic turn-scoped input must not be treated as session-scoped pending work.
Promotion must be an ordered, once-only transition (promoted_seq guards).
failurePolicy: fail-closed - a divergent projection dies with LifecycleConflict.
